title: Davidoff Cool Water vs Creed Green Irish Tweed: Which Should You Wear?
summary: The same perfumer composed Davidoff Cool Water and Creed Green Irish Tweed three years apart. Compare their notes, longevity, and which suits you.
body_markdown:
One perfumer built both of these fragrances, three years and two very different market positions apart: Pierre Bourdon is widely credited with composing Creed Green Irish Tweed in 1985, then[Davidoff Cool Water](https://www.scentbird.com/perfume/davidoff-cool-water-1578) in 1988.


Davidoff Cool Water, available on Scentbird.


## What Cool Water and Green Irish Tweed Share


Both fragrances carry a version of the same perfumer’s preference for restraint over sweetness, and a clean, uncluttered structure instead of a long note list. Both were also aimed at a similar idea of understated masculinity rather than anything loud or spiced, and both have stayed in continuous production for decades without a major reformulation overhaul. Beyond that shared authorship, the two part ways almost immediately: one is built around abstract iris and violet, the other around a literal splash of cold, mentholated water. It helps explain why fragrance forums keep bringing this pairing up: the family resemblance is real, even if the price points and distribution could not be further apart.


## Davidoff Cool Water: A Closer Look


Picture a cold rinse after cutting the grass on a summer morning: spearmint and sea water arrive first, green and a little sharp, before anything softer has a chance to show up. Coriander smooths that edge briefly, then geranium, jasmine, and neroli carry the middle before the fragrance settles into sandalwood, musk, a trace of oakmoss, and tobacco. It holds for about 4 to 6 hours on most skin, with projection that’s noticeable early and pulls close after the first hour or two. Skip it if you’re drawn to the softer, more abstract green character Green Irish Tweed builds around iris instead of mint.


## Creed Green Irish Tweed: A Closer Look


Green Irish Tweed came three years earlier, in 1985, historically credited to Olivier Creed though Pierre Bourdon is now widely recognized as its actual composer. It opens on lemon verbena and iris, cooler and more abstract than Cool Water’s literal sea water accord, then moves into violet leaf for a soft, powdery green heart. A base of ambergris and sandalwood stays close to the skin rather than projecting outward, giving the whole thing a quieter, more refined character. On most skin it holds for about 5 to 7 hours, a bit longer than Cool Water, though its sillage stays intimate throughout instead of announcing itself. Skip it if you want a fragrance that reads clearly from a few feet away, since this one was composed to stay close to the skin rather than fill a room.


## Cool Water vs Green Irish Tweed at a Glance


Davidoff Cool Water Green Irish Tweed


Feel Bright, minty, aquatic Soft, powdery, green-iris


Main notes Sea water, lavender, sandalwood, musk Lemon verbena, iris, violet leaf, ambergris


Lasts About 4 to 6 hours About 5 to 7 hours


Best for Casual daily wear, warm weather Understated, smart-casual settings


## So Which One Should You Actually Wear?


The key differentiator is how the same perfumer’s instincts show up in two directions. Cool Water takes that instinct for restraint and makes it loud and literal with mint and cold water, built for daily, casual wear that doesn’t ask the wearer to think twice before spraying it on. Green Irish Tweed takes a related sensibility and turns it abstract and soft, built around iris and violet leaf that stay close to the skin rather than project outward. If you want the more accessible, obviously fresh version of that shared idea, Cool Water is it. If you want the quieter, more refined side of the same perfumer’s work, Green Irish Tweed is built for that instead. Setting matters too: a busy office or a crowded gathering suits Green Irish Tweed’s close sillage, while an outdoor afternoon gives Cool Water’s brighter opening somewhere to actually project.


Verdict


Choose Cool Water for an easy, literal freshness that suits daily wear and warm weather. Choose Green Irish Tweed when you want something softer and more abstract that reads as understated up close rather than obvious from across a room. Both trace back to the same perfumer’s hand, just aimed at different moods.


Let a month of daily wear answer the question for you.

## Frequently Asked Questions


Did the same perfumer make Cool Water and Green Irish Tweed?


Yes. Pierre Bourdon is widely credited as the composer behind both, working on Green Irish Tweed for Creed in 1985 and then Davidoff Cool Water three years later, in 1988. Despite the shared hand, the two fragrances take very different approaches.


Is Green Irish Tweed similar to Cool Water?


Only in spirit, not in notes. Both favor restraint over sweetness, but Green Irish Tweed builds that restraint around abstract iris and violet leaf, while Cool Water builds it around a literal, cold splash of mint and sea water. They read as related but distinct.


Which lasts longer, Cool Water or Green Irish Tweed?


Green Irish Tweed tends to last a bit longer, around 5 to 7 hours compared to about 4 to 6 hours for Cool Water. Neither projects aggressively, though Green Irish Tweed stays especially close to the skin throughout its wear.


Is Creed Green Irish Tweed available on Scentbird?


No, Green Irish Tweed is included here only as a point of comparison. Davidoff Cool Water is available on Scentbird, so it is the fragrance you can try directly through a monthly subscription.


What is the main difference between Cool Water and Green Irish Tweed?


Cool Water is loud and literal, opening on mint and sea water for an immediate sense of coldness. Green Irish Tweed is quieter and more abstract, built on iris and violet leaf that stay soft and close to the skin rather than announcing themselves.


Which is more office-appropriate, Cool Water or Green Irish Tweed?


Green Irish Tweed edges ahead here thanks to its quiet, close-to-skin sillage, which rarely intrudes on a shared workspace. Cool Water works fine too, but its brighter mint opening is a touch more noticeable in the first hour.
